text:
maria: :rotating_light: APAC egress + provisioning anomalies — ap-northeast1 GPU pools reporting high egress latency and ~25-35% provisioning failures since 08:02 UTC. Customers hitting longer cold-starts and some requests 504ing. Investigating now.
oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-042 APAC egress/provisioning — assigned to @ashwin oncall. Runbook pinned: /runbooks/apac-provisioning-failures
ashwin: seeing the alerts. jstack of prober shows many `attach elasticip timeout` and `pod pulled but not ready` errors. can someone confirm if this is network-nat or cloud-provider side?
jordan: from control-plane logs: provisioning failures correlate with upstream TCP RSTs to our provisioning agents. Also seeing UDP path MTU blackholes to a subset of tokyo ISPs. 30% of new GPU clients fail init within 30s.
lee: checked BGP sessions to ISP-A in tokyo. intermittent flaps started ~07:58 UTC, routes oscillating. ISP reports they see packet drops on their egress cluster. we're initiating failover to ISP-B for affected AZs and flipping NAT gateways to secondary.
maria: can we traffic-shift to ap-southeast1 for latency-sensitive customers while we stabilize tokyo? rough ETA to get partial routing in place?
ashwin: I can push route policy in 10m for dedicated reserved pools and 20-30m for shared-hosted by tagging critical tenants. That should cut error rate by ~80% for those traffic flows.
jordan: will update autoscaler to prefer ap-southeast1 for new allocations and drain ap-northeast1 GPU pools. draining may take ~15-25m depending on KV cache warmups.
support-sara: prepping customer comms. Suggest we post statuspage and do targeted pings to customers with SLA impacted workloads. Proposed public message: "We are aware of provisioning and egress issues impacting APAC (ap-northeast1). Engineers are actively failing over traffic and we estimate mitigation for most customers within 90 minutes. Updates every 15 minutes." ok?
maria: agree to 90m ETA but caveat: dependent on ISP stabilization. also add workaround: customers can pin to ap-southeast1 or request manual failover via support ticket to prioritize.
lee: NAT flip started. initial telemetry shows drop in RSTs for 50% of flows. continuing.
ashwin: routing policy staged for critical tenants. cost note: moving significant traffic cross-region will increase egress and inter-region replication costs — ballpark additional $3-6k/hr if we shift full shared workload. flagging for finance FYI.
jordan: can do hybrid: only shift low-latency and high-qps tenants; leave batch jobs on ap-northeast1 to avoid extra egress. that halves cost estimate.
support-sara: posted draft to statuspage, setting incident as "partial outage" and adding ETA 90m. Will ping top 20 enterprise contacts now.
statuspage-bot: Status page update posted: "Investigating — APAC provisioning & egress degradation. Engineers working on routing failover and mitigations. Next update in 15 minutes." https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-2026-042
maria: thanks team. priority: 1) stabilize customer-facing paths, 2) minimize cost by selective routing, 3) clear comms. keep updates here. I'll coordinate postmortem owner once stable.
lee: NAT flip complete for ISP-B path for 2/3 affected AZs. provisioning failures down to ~8% in those AZs.
ashwin: incremental rollout to remaining AZ in 7m. starting now.
support-sara: escalations: two enterprise customers opened high-priority tickets requesting ETA and whether failover will impact data locality. replying with the statuspage link and offer manual failover.
maria: good. reminder: log the tenants we manually fail over and include in postmortem scope (cost + quality delta).
jordan: current plan: full mitigation for critical tenants in ~35m, broader mitigation in ~90m. I'll update statuspage in 15.
statuspage-bot: Next update scheduled at 08:35 UTC."
